summary: Put the products on the store(s) in their tree category: the products whose
description: tree categories are not their node's term — e.g. filed under a parent before their category was created on the store, or every product on a store's first Apply (linking a term moves nothing by itself). Categories outside the tree (Clearance, Open Box …) are kept. Per-serial guns count as products and are counted apart (``by_doctype``). Limit: a product's full push (and the catalog feed's re-categorise) still writes its tree category alone, dropping Clearance / Open Box — only this catch-up keeps them.

args.name: site
args.desc: "retail" (the only store); empty = every store that follows the tree.

args.name: dry_run
args.desc: 1 (default) reports only; 0 moves them in a background job (category only, paced; a product the store refuses lands in the Error Log).

args.name: under
args.desc: node slugs (a list, JSON list or comma-separated) — only the products filed in their subtrees; empty = the whole store.

returns: {site: {checked, to_move, by_doctype: {Item, Serial No}, moves: [{doctype, now, want, count, sample: [product ids]}] (grouped by the tree categories now → the one to get, largest first), no_term, no_node, gone, sample: [{doctype, name, item, product_id, category, now, want, set}] (the first 50)}};…

Returns per-serial results and any errors encountered. .. note:: **Aggregating semantics** — every serial is attempted regardless of earlier failures; errors are collected and returned rather than re-raised. This differs from :func:`ffl_woo_sync.woocommerce.sync.push_all_serials` which is fail-fast (re-raises the first per-serial exception immediately).

description: Routing is determined server-side so all callers (Item form button, MCP, future automation) behave correctly without any client-side detection: - **Per-serial firearm** (``is_firearm=1``, ``uniform_sell_price=0``): pushes every Active Serial No via :func:`ffl_woo_sync.woocommerce.sync.push_serial`. Returns ``{"ok": bool, "pushed": [...], "errors": [...], "skipped": [...], "total": int}``. This branch does **not** pass ``_relist``: a hidden gun stays hidden and lands in ``skipped`` (an Item-level bulk relist would also revive guns hidden one-by-one for holds or repairs). The per-gun route is t…

summary: Push the item product + all Active serials in a single call.
description: Uses a shared client and pre-fetched attribute IDs. Returns combined results: the item push result plus per-serial results and any errors. Suitable for "initial listing" of a per-serial firearm item where you want to bring everything live in one operation. FULL-PAYLOAD by design: as a deliberate, confirmed bulk action it keeps the manual-push semantics — which means it WILL overwrite wp-admin content edits (title / description / images) with the POS versions on every product it touches. Routine drift healing belongs to the scheduled reconcile, which is pos_fields_only and content-safe.

summary: Re-push ONLY the attributes to existing retail Woo firearm products.
description: The attributes are Caliber / Condition / Manufacturer / Model. Fixes stale ``pa_condition`` terms after a grade / ``is_used`` correction in POS: lean machine pushes never carry attributes, so they never get there on their own. The payload is exactly ``{"attributes": [...]}`` per product — name, description, images, price, stock and meta are never sent, and no POS record is written. Products on the shop that were hidden (``woo_delisted``) or never listed are skipped. Attributes are authoritative on a PUT: any attribute on the product other than those four is removed. Run with ``dry_run=1`` fir…

args.name: item_codes

returns: ``{"pushed": n, "skipped": n, "errors": n, "dry_run": bool, "would_push": n, "skipped_by_reason": {...}, "error_details": [...]}`` — ``pushed`` is products the store accepted; with ``dry_run`` it is 0 and ``would_push`` counts the products that would be sent.

summary: Audit stored Woo product ids for ones whose WC product was deleted (404).
description: Scans every connected store by default, and a store it cannot build a client for is reported as skipped rather than aborting the run: letting the config error out of here would 500 the request AND roll back any repairs already made in the same transaction.

args.name: fix
args.desc: Report-only by default; 1 (or True) nulls each dangling id and leaves a Comment + warning log.

args.name: batch_size
args.desc: Clamped to 1..200; bounds each verification chunk — a fat-finger clamp on the parameter, not a rate limit; every candidate is checked.

args.name: site
args.desc: Limits to one store — "retail", the only one (default: all).

returns: { "checked": <int>, # ids verified against WooCommerce "dangling": [{"doctype","name","field","site","woo_id"}, ...], "fixed": <int>, # ids nulled (0 unless fix) "skipped": [{"site","reason"}, ...], # stores with no usable client "counts": {"by_doctype": {...}, "by_site": {...}}, }

Idempotent via the {serial, woo_online_order} guard. Refuses an in-store pickup — an order whose receiving FFL is this store's own licence (``FFL Settings.own_ffl_license``). There is no far-end dealer to transfer to; the buyer collects at the counter under a retail 4473, and booking it here would write…

summary: List web invoices whose accessory stock never left — the month-end control.

Before closing a month, call this for that month (first to last day) and expect an empty list: a web invoice whose accessory Delivery Note never posted still shows a cost in the Sales Report (its cost column is qty x Bin valuation rate, not the GL), so the report cannot reveal the gap and its cost can only be trusted against GL COGS once this is empty. A non-zero count lists the invoices: run ``run_web_revenue_backstop_now`` to issue the ones that can be issued, handle the rest by hand. Also before closing: no open ToDo on a Sales Invoice or Woo Online Order from this machinery (a…

The web order deliberately STAYS in the Pending Order queue until that counter invoice is submitted (see :func:`close_web_order_on_pos_submit`). description: A shipped firearm with no disposition is a missing A&D entry, and nothing surfaced it before — the seven such orders on 2026-08-14 were found by hand. Reports only; it never disposes anything. Which rifle went in the box is exactly what POS does not know in this state, and guessing it is the mistake the whole serial-handling rework exists to stop.
returns: {checked, reported} — `reported` is 0 when the daily throttle suppressed an otherwise non-empty report.

summary: Re-apply the serial WooCommerce still holds to rows stuck on a STALE
description: ``reservation_error``. A rejection is a snapshot of the moment it was written ("that gun is held by WOO-ORD-x"). The only thing that ever retried it was the next ``order.updated`` webhook — so when the obstacle cleared (the other order cancelled, or swapped to a different gun) nothing re-ran, and a Woo order that has gone ``completed`` sends no further webhook. The row then sat in the Pending Order queue indefinitely, quoting a reason that had stopped being true, and staff had no way to clear it but to re-save the serial on Woo. (2026-08-07: WOO-ORD-01488 was refused C2322, which WOO-ORD-0149…
returns: A summary dict (retried / cleared / aged-out / skipped counts) so a manual run says what it did.
